tooltip.toolbar.modeToggle: Beginner shows essential and common Inspector sections. Pro also shows advanced and diagnostic sections. Remembered per-user.

tooltip.toolbar.snap: Snaps move/resize/create operations to the grid size below.
tooltip.toolbar.rebuild: Rebuilds the live preview from scratch (backend elements + bindings + theme + motion) - use if the canvas looks out of sync with the metadata.
tooltip.toolbar.save: Saves the Studio metadata and the open Screen asset.
tooltip.toolbar.validate: Re-runs all project validators (duplicate ids, missing assets, backend mismatches, ...) against the open screen.
tooltip.toolbar.distributeH: Space 3+ selected elements evenly along the horizontal axis.
tooltip.toolbar.distributeV: Space 3+ selected elements evenly along the vertical axis.
tooltip.toolbar.bringForward: Move the selected element one step forward (toward the front) in draw order.
tooltip.toolbar.sendBackward: Move the selected element one step backward (toward the back) in draw order.
tooltip.toolbar.bringToFront: Move the selected element to the very front of the draw order.
tooltip.toolbar.sendToBack: Move the selected element to the very back of the draw order.
tooltip.style.id: Unique id used by binding keys, commandKeys, and backend name-matching (UXML/GameObject name). Renaming this repoints child parentIds automatically.
tooltip.style.displayName: Human-readable label shown in the Hierarchy panel. Purely cosmetic - does not affect runtime lookup.
tooltip.style.type: Semantic element type (Panel, Button, Label, ...). Drives the default backend visual and which capabilities the runtime expects it to expose.
tooltip.style.text: Static preview text for Label/Button-like elements. Overridden at runtime by binding.textKey if one is set.
tooltip.style.classes: Space-separated style classes applied to this element (USS classes for UI Toolkit, or the equivalent class-toggle set for uGUI).
tooltip.style.shape: Studio-canvas preview shape for this element's box: Rectangle (square corners), Rounded (small radius, the previous default), Pill (fully rounded ends), or Circle/Ellipse. Preview only - does not change the backend UXML/prefab's own styling.
tooltip.style.previewValue: Fill amount shown in the Studio canvas for this Progress Bar/Stat Bar/Radial Fill, in the Min/Max range below (preview only - the real value at runtime comes from binding.valueKey).
tooltip.style.minValue: Lower bound of the preview value range, matching Unity Slider's minValue (e.g. 0).
tooltip.style.maxValue: Upper bound of the preview value range, matching Unity Slider's maxValue (e.g. 100).
tooltip.style.fillDirection: Which edge the fill grows from, matching Unity Image's FillMethod + fillOrigin (Horizontal/Left,Right or Vertical/Bottom,Top).
tooltip.style.clockwise: Sweep direction of the radial fill/spin arc, matching Unity Image's fillClockwise.
tooltip.style.previewImage: Texture shown in the Studio canvas for this Image/Icon Button (preview only - the backend UXML/prefab keeps its own sprite/texture reference).
tooltip.style.tint: Background/graphic tint color shown in the Studio preview and applied to the backend element.
tooltip.style.fontSize: Font size in points, clamped to 8-96.
tooltip.style.hidden: Hides this element in the Studio canvas only (does not affect runtime visibility) - use to declutter the canvas without deleting metadata.
tooltip.layout.position: Top-left position in canvas pixels (absolute, not relative to the parent element).
tooltip.layout.size: Width/height in canvas pixels. Clamped to a 24px minimum on each axis.
tooltip.layout.anchor: uGUI-style anchor preset applied to the backend RectTransform/style on save (Stretch fills the parent on that axis).
tooltip.layout.locked: Prevents move/resize/rect edits on the canvas (Inspector fields still work) - use to avoid accidentally dragging a finished element.
tooltip.binding.textKey: UIStateStore key whose string value drives this element's text at runtime (via UITextBinder). Leave empty for static text.
tooltip.binding.valueKey: UIStateStore key whose float value drives this element's Value capability at runtime (progress bars, sliders).
tooltip.binding.visibilityKey: UIStateStore key whose bool value shows/hides this element at runtime.
tooltip.binding.classKey: UIStateStore key whose string value is applied as a style class at runtime (for state-driven styling, e.g. "selected"/"error").
tooltip.binding.commandKey: Action key executed when this element is clicked - resolved through a UIActionResolver at runtime (see UICommandBinder). Use Pick... to reuse a key already wired elsewhere instead of typing a new one.
tooltip.binding.interactableKey: UIStateStore key whose bool value enables/disables interaction on this element at runtime.
tooltip.binding.pickData: Connect this binding key to a data-source IBindableProperty<T> found by reflection.
tooltip.binding.pickCommand: Choose from built-in pipeline commands or commandKeys already used elsewhere in this project.
tooltip.theme.themeAsset: Optional direct theme asset reference. Assigning one also seeds Theme Id below from the asset's themeId, if empty.
tooltip.theme.themeId: Theme id string used to resolve theme tokens at runtime, independent of the direct asset reference above (useful when the theme is swapped at runtime via NexUITheme.Use).
tooltip.theme.classes: Space-separated theme-specific style classes, applied in addition to the Style section's Classes field.
tooltip.theme.addToken: Overrides a single theme token (e.g. "color.primary") for this element only, without touching the shared theme asset.
tooltip.theme.eyedropperColor: Click the swatch to open Unity's color picker - it has a built-in eyedropper to sample any pixel on screen. Then press "Add as Token".
tooltip.theme.addEyedropperToken: Adds the color on the left as a new token override (name the key afterward).
tooltip.theme.tokenValue: Override value for this token, on this element only.
tooltip.motion.preset: The compiled motion asset (built with the Motion Graph editor) this element animates with.
tooltip.motion.motionId: Identifier used to look up this motion at runtime; seeded from the preset's own motionId when one is assigned.
tooltip.motion.initial: Variant name applied the instant this element becomes visible (before any animation plays).
tooltip.motion.animate: Variant name played when the element enters (e.g. screen open).
tooltip.motion.exit: Variant name played when the element exits (e.g. screen close).
tooltip.motion.hover: Variant name played on pointer hover, if the backend/capability supports it.
tooltip.motion.pressed: Variant name played while the element is pressed/held.
tooltip.motion.focus: Variant name played while the element has keyboard/gamepad focus.
tooltip.motion.openGraph: Opens the visual node-graph editor for the assigned preset.
tooltip.motion.openClipEditor: Opens the timeline clip editor scoped to this specific element in the live preview.
tooltip.policy.inputBlocking: Blocks pointer/gamepad input to screens behind this one while it's open.
tooltip.policy.pauseGameBehind: Pauses gameplay (Time.timeScale-style) while this screen is open.
tooltip.policy.closeOnBack: Closes this screen when the Back command (Cancel/Escape) fires.
tooltip.policy.cursorPolicy: Cursor visibility/lock state to force while this screen is open (Unchanged leaves whatever the game already set).
tooltip.policy.timePolicy: Whether opening this screen pauses or slows game time.
tooltip.policy.focusPolicy: Keyboard/gamepad focus behavior on open - AutoFocusDefault focuses focus.defaultFocusElementId; TrapFocus additionally prevents Tab from leaving the screen.
tooltip.policy.conflictPolicy: What happens if this screen is asked to open/close again while a transition is already playing.
tooltip.policy.lifetimePolicy: Whether the screen instance is destroyed, kept alive, or pooled when closed.
tooltip.accessibility.label: Screen-reader-facing label for this element. Falls back to Text/Name at runtime when empty.
tooltip.accessibility.role: Semantic role hint (Button, Toggle, Slider, ...) for screen-reader/switch-control bridges, following the common ARIA/UIKit role vocabulary.
tooltip.autoLayout.enabled: Arranges this element's direct children along one axis (Figma-style Auto Layout), instead of each child keeping an independent absolute rect.
tooltip.autoLayout.direction: Axis children are arranged along - Row (left to right) or Column (top to bottom).
tooltip.autoLayout.spacing: Gap between consecutive children along the direction axis, in pixels.
tooltip.autoLayout.paddingLeft: Inset from this element's left edge to its children.
tooltip.autoLayout.paddingTop: Inset from this element's top edge to its children.
tooltip.autoLayout.paddingRight: Inset from this element's right edge to its children.
tooltip.autoLayout.paddingBottom: Inset from this element's bottom edge to its children.
tooltip.autoLayout.widthSizing: How this element sizes horizontally when its parent is an Auto Layout container: Fixed (use its own rect width), Hug (fit content), or Fill (grow to take remaining space).
tooltip.autoLayout.heightSizing: How this element sizes vertically when its parent is an Auto Layout container: Fixed (use its own rect height), Hug (fit content), or Fill (grow to take remaining space).
tooltip.constraints.horizontal: Pin behavior on the horizontal axis when the parent is resized: Start (left), End (right), Center, or Scale (resize proportionally).
tooltip.constraints.vertical: Pin behavior on the vertical axis when the parent is resized: Start (top), End (bottom), Center, or Scale (resize proportionally).
tooltip.capability.list: Runtime capability interfaces (IUI*Capability) this element type is expected to expose - informational, derived from the Type field in the Style section.
tooltip.multiSelection.summary: Number of elements in the current multi-selection.
tooltip.multiSelection.position: Shared position across the selection, or "Mixed" if they differ.
tooltip.multiSelection.size: Shared size across the selection, or "Mixed" if they differ.
tooltip.multiSelection.layer: Draw-order index range covered by the selection (contiguous elements only), or "Mixed" otherwise.
tooltip.validation.text: This element's data is checked against these four categories whenever validation runs - see the Validation panel below for the actual issue list.
tooltip.screenDefinition.screen: The UIScreenDefinition asset currently open (read-only here - use the toolbar's Screen field to switch).
tooltip.palette.search: Filter the component list by name.
tooltip.palette.addComponent: Add a {0} element to the current screen.
tooltip.palette.alignLeft: Align the selected element's left edge to the canvas.
tooltip.palette.alignCenterX: Center the selected element horizontally on the canvas.
tooltip.palette.alignRight: Align the selected element's right edge to the canvas.
tooltip.palette.alignTop: Align the selected element's top edge to the canvas.
tooltip.palette.alignCenterY: Center the selected element vertically on the canvas.
tooltip.palette.alignBottom: Align the selected element's bottom edge to the canvas.
tooltip.palette.fill: Resize the selected element to fill the entire canvas resolution.
tooltip.palette.copy: Duplicate the selected element(s), offset slightly from the original.
tooltip.palette.delete: Delete the selected element(s). This does not delete their children - reparent those first if needed.
tooltip.hierarchy.search: Filter elements by id or display name.
tooltip.hierarchy.visibility: Toggle visibility in the Studio canvas (does not affect runtime visibility).
tooltip.hierarchy.lock: Toggle locked (prevents move/resize/rect edits on the canvas).
tooltip.state.title: Lists every UIStateStore binding key wired on the selected element (or every element, if none is selected).
tooltip.state.filter: Filter the binding key list below by substring.
tooltip.state.keys: elementId / binding kind = UIStateStore key, for every binding on the selected element (or all elements).
tooltip.command.title: Preview/edit the selected element's commandKey (the action dispatched when it's clicked at runtime).
tooltip.command.field: Command key for the selected element. Editing here is the same as the Binding inspector's Command Key field.
tooltip.command.run: Preview-dispatch this command key (does not actually invoke the runtime Command Pipeline - just previews the key that would be sent) and save it onto the selected element.
tooltip.screenGraph.title: C1 command/binding link view: with nothing selected, summarizes the screen (backend, variant/responsive-rule/element counts); with an element selected, shows exactly which commandKey/textKey/valueKey/etc. it's wired to.
tooltip.validationPanel.title: Results from every registered project validator (duplicate ids, missing assets, backend mismatches, ...), re-run on Validate or whenever the metadata changes.
tooltip.validationPanel.item: Click to select "{0}" in the Hierarchy/canvas.
motionClip.toolbar.noClip: Create or assign a Motion Clip to begin.
motionClip.toolbar.noTracks: No tracks yet. Select an element in the Studio and click "Add Track".
motionClip.status.label: Status
tooltip.motionClip.clipField: The Motion Clip asset being edited. Assign or create one to start adding tracks.
tooltip.motionClip.createClip: Creates a new empty Motion Clip asset and opens it here.
tooltip.motionClip.addTrackFromSelection: Adds a track targeting the element currently selected in the NexUI Studio.
tooltip.motionClip.duration: Total length of the clip, in seconds. Keyframes beyond this time are clamped when played.
tooltip.motionClip.fps: Frames-per-second used for the timeline's frame display and for Snap.
tooltip.motionClip.loop: When enabled, playback restarts from 0 instead of stopping at the end.
tooltip.motionClip.snap: When enabled, dragging or typing a keyframe's time snaps it to the nearest frame (1 / FPS seconds).
tooltip.motionClip.play: Plays the clip from the current scrub position against the connected preview surface.
tooltip.motionClip.save: Saves all changes to the Motion Clip asset to disk.
tooltip.motionClip.scrubber: Drag to scrub the preview time. Evaluates the clip at this time on the connected preview surface.
tooltip.motionClip.addPropertyTrack: Adds a track for the selected property, so it can be animated for this element.
tooltip.motionClip.addKeyframe: Adds a keyframe at the current scrub time, using the element's current value.
tooltip.motionClip.deleteTrack: Removes this property track (and all its keyframes) from the element.
tooltip.motionClip.lockTrack: Locks this track so its keyframes can't be added, moved, or deleted from the canvas or timeline.
tooltip.motionClip.keyframeDot: Click to select. Shift-click to range-select, Ctrl/Cmd-click to toggle. Drag to move (all selected keyframes move together). Right-click to delete.
tooltip.motionClip.openDesigner: Opens the NexUI Studio window so a screen can be loaded as the preview surface.
tooltip.motionClip.reason.noClip: Create or assign a Motion Clip first.
tooltip.motionClip.reason.noElementSelec: Select an element in the NexUI Studio first.
tooltip.motionClip.reason.noPropertyTrac: Add at least one property track first.
tooltip.motionClip.reason.trackLocked: This track is locked. Click Unlock to edit it.
tooltip.motionClip.reason.nothingToStop: Playback is already stopped and nothing needs restoring.
tooltip.motionClip.stop: Stops playback, rewinds to 0, and restores every animated element to its pre-preview pose.
tooltip.motionClip.autoKey: Off: canvas edits only change layout. Existing Tracks: canvas edits update keyframes on tracks that already exist. All Changes: canvas edits also create the track/property track if missing.
tooltip.motionClip.recording: Auto Key is on: moving or resizing this element on the NexUI Studio canvas writes a keyframe at the current scrub time instead of only updating its layout.
tooltip.motionClip.easingButton: Opens the Easing Browser to pick how this keyframe blends into the next one.
tooltip.motionClip.customCurve: Hand-drawn curve for this keyframe (drag the tangent handles). Overrides the Easing selection above.
easing.hint.Basic: Constant speed, or a gentle smoothed start/end. Safe default for most UI motion.
easing.hint.Cubic: Moderate acceleration/deceleration - a common general-purpose choice.
easing.hint.Quintic: Very strong acceleration/deceleration - snappy, almost abrupt.
easing.hint.Sine: The gentlest curve of the set. Good for natural, calm enter/exit motion.
easing.hint.Exponential: Sharp acceleration. Good for fast pop-ins or teleport-like motion.
easing.hint.Back: Overshoots the target slightly before settling. Recommended for: Modal entrances, Button Pop, drawing attention to a notification.
easing.hint.Elastic: Springs back and forth like elastic before settling. Recommended for: playful emphasis, reward/success feedback.
easing.hint.Bounce: Settles like a ball bouncing to a stop.
easing.hint.Custom: Draw your own curve for this keyframe instead of picking a named easing.
tooltip.motionClip.scaleTimingFactor: Multiplier used by Scale Timing below (e.g. 2 doubles every keyframe's time, 0.5 halves it). Times are clamped to the clip's duration.
tooltip.motionClip.moreTrackOps: Copy/paste keyframes between compatible tracks, reverse this track's timing, or scale it by the factor to the left.
tooltip.viewport.motionPath: Shows the selected element's travel path and keyframes. The original UI remains at the start with reduced opacity while the live UI moves to the evaluated destination.
tooltip.viewport.onionSkin: Adds nearby before/after keyframe ghosts in addition to the persistent start pose, so motion spacing can be judged without scrubbing back and forth.
tooltip.motionClip.useWorkArea: When Loop is also on, only the first playback pass plays the full clip; every pass after that repeats just the Start-End range below (e.g. an intro followed by a looping idle segment).
tooltip.motionClip.addMarker: Adds a named marker at the current scrub time (e.g. "Impact", "Loop Point"). Right-click a marker to rename or delete it.
tooltip.motionClip.markerFlag: Click to jump the scrub time here. Right-click to rename or delete.
stateMachine.toolbar.noMachine: Create or assign a Motion State Machine to begin.
tooltip.stateMachine.asset: The Motion State Machine asset being edited. Assign or create one to start adding transitions.
tooltip.stateMachine.create: Creates a new empty Motion State Machine asset and opens it here.
tooltip.stateMachine.defaultState: The state a component using this machine starts in before any transition runs.
tooltip.stateMachine.addTransition: Adds a new From -> To transition. Assign a clip and pick an Interrupt Policy for it.
tooltip.stateMachine.anyState: When on, this transition matches a change to the To state from any current state (the From dropdown is ignored).
tooltip.stateMachine.interruptPolicy: Restart: cancel and replay from scratch. Ignore: drop the request if a transition is already playing. Complete Immediately: snap the interrupted clip to its end pose first, then play this one.
tooltip.stateMachine.preview: Plays this transition's clip against the connected NexUI Studio preview surface, exactly like the Motion Clip Editor's Play button.
tooltip.stateMachine.reason.noClip: Assign a clip to this transition first.
graphV2.toolbar.noAsset: No Motion Graph assigned. Pick or create one above.
tooltip.graphV2.preview: Runs the selected event through the graph against the connected NexUI Studio preview surface - a real execution, using the selected canvas element (if any) as the Current Event Target.
focusNav.panel.title: Focus Navigation
tooltip.focusNav.autoGenerate: Computes Up/Down/Left/Right links for every element on this screen from their canvas positions (nearest neighbor in each direction). Overwrites any links already authored.
tooltip.focusNav.defaultFocus: The element a gamepad/keyboard cursor starts on when this screen opens. At most one element per screen should have this on.
tooltip.viewport.focusNav: Shows every authored gamepad/keyboard navigation link on the canvas as a line between elements, and marks the screen's default focus element.
scenario.window.title: Scenario
scenario.window.description: Edit a mock-state scenario and apply it to the open screen, or capture the current preview state into a scenario.
scenario.field.name: Name
scenario.help.noAsset: Select or create a scenario asset.
tooltip.scenario.asset: The DesignerScenarioAsset to edit. Like a Motion Clip, it is a standalone asset so scenarios can be reused across screens and checked into source control.
tooltip.scenario.create: Creates a new DesignerScenarioAsset in the project.
tooltip.scenario.name: Scenario name (e.g. Inventory Empty, Low Health).
tooltip.scenario.description: Notes on the state this scenario reproduces.
tooltip.scenario.addBinding: Adds a mock binding value. Key is a state/binding key; it drives the preview value, text, or visibility of every element bound to that key.
tooltip.scenario.forcedState: On apply, forces every component into this preview state. None leaves the state untouched.
tooltip.scenario.language: On apply, switches the Studio language. None leaves the language untouched.
tooltip.scenario.apply: Applies this scenario to the open screen - writes each mock value into the preview channels of elements bound to that key. A single Undo reverts the whole thing. Never runs game commands.
tooltip.scenario.capture: Captures the current screen's preview state (per-element binding value/text/visibility, forced state, language) into this scenario.
tooltip.scenario.save: Saves the edited scenario asset to disk.
tooltip.scenario.timeline.use: Enables a timeline whose mock values change over time (e.g. 0s health 100 → 2s health 15). Play/scrub drives the canvas live.
tooltip.scenario.timeline.loop: Restart from the beginning when the end is reached.
tooltip.scenario.timeline.scrub: Moves the playhead and applies the timeline state at that time to the canvas. Numeric keys interpolate linearly between neighbors; Bool/Text keys step. Stop restores the original preview values.
tooltip.scenario.timeline.addKey: Adds a timeline key at the current time. Key is a state/binding key; it sets that key's value at this moment.
scenario.record.help: While recording, element edits in the Studio (bound value/text/visibility changes) are saved as timeline keys with their elapsed time. Stop, then replay the timeline to reproduce them.
tooltip.scenario.record.start: Records the current screen's element edits as timeline keys from now on. Existing timeline keys are cleared and the starting state is captured at t=0.
tooltip.scenario.record.stop: Stops recording and trims the timeline duration to the last key.
screenFlow.status.noAsset: Select or create a Screen Flow asset
tooltip.screenFlow.asset: The DesignerScreenFlowAsset to edit. A standalone asset representing screens as nodes and navigation as typed transitions (Push/Pop/Replace/Overlay/Modal/Return).
tooltip.screenFlow.create: Creates a new DesignerScreenFlowAsset in the project.
tooltip.screenFlow.addNode: Adds a screen node at the center of the graph. Set its screen id and kind (Screen/Overlay/Modal/HUD/Subflow) on the node.
tooltip.screenFlow.autoLayout: Lays nodes out left-to-right by transition distance from the entry node.
tooltip.screenFlow.setEntry: Marks the selected node as this flow's entry node.
tooltip.screenFlow.validate: Checks for broken/dangling transitions, nodes unreachable from the entry, and missing screen assignments.
tooltip.screenFlow.save: Saves the edited Screen Flow asset to disk.
uxmlGen.window.title: Generate UXML/USS
uxmlGen.window.description: Generates UXML and USS from the open screen's Studio metadata. It never touches a hand-authored source UXML - it only writes separate generated files (.g.uxml/.g.uss).
uxmlGen.help.noScreen: Open a UI Toolkit screen in the main Studio.
uxmlGen.help.safety: Generation reads metadata; writing only saves to separate files next to the metadata asset (<screen>.g.uxml / .g.uss). Existing files without the generated banner are never overwritten.
uxmlGen.dialog.refuseOverwrite: A target file already exists and is not a NexUI-generated file. Write was cancelled to protect your hand-authored file.
tooltip.uxmlGen.generate: Generates UXML/USS text from the current screen metadata and previews it below. No files are written yet.
tooltip.uxmlGen.write: Writes the previewed UXML/USS to separate generated files (.g.uxml/.g.uss). The source UXML is never touched.
tokens.window.title: Design Tokens
tokens.window.description: Create design tokens (color, spacing, radius, motion, ...), alias one token to another, and see each token's resolved value.
tokens.help.noAsset: Select or create a token set asset.
tooltip.tokens.asset: The DesignerTokenSetAsset to edit. Like a Theme, it is a standalone asset holding color/spacing/radius/motion tokens.
tooltip.tokens.create: Creates a new DesignerTokenSetAsset in the project.
tooltip.tokens.add: Adds a token. Depending on category it holds a color/number/string value, and can reference (alias) another token.
accessibility.audit.title: Screen Accessibility Audit
accessibility.audit.noScreen: Open a screen in the main Studio to audit contrast, touch targets, and labels/roles.
sync.window.title: Sync & Publish
sync.window.description: Three-way compares generated UXML/USS against the on-disk files and the last published baseline. Distinguishes Studio/backend changes and conflicts, and publishes only changed screens.
sync.help.noManifest: Without a publish manifest there is no baseline, so conflicts cannot be distinguished (changed/unchanged only). Create a manifest.
sync.help.noScreen: Open a screen in the main Studio.
sync.dialog.blocked: The target file is not a generated file, so it was not overwritten (shown as backend-changed/conflict).
tooltip.sync.manifest: The DesignerPublishManifest holding each screen's last-published content hashes - the baseline of the three-way comparison.
tooltip.sync.useDesigner: Writes the generated UXML/USS to the files and records them as the baseline. Files without the generated banner are not overwritten.
tooltip.sync.useBackend: Adopts the on-disk files as the new baseline (clears conflict/backend-changed without regenerating).
tooltip.sync.reviewDiff: Shows the line-level difference between the file and the generated result (+ added, - removed).
tooltip.sync.dryRun: Reports, without writing, whether each screen would be published / skipped / needs resolution.
tooltip.sync.publish: Writes only New/Studio-changed screens. In-sync is skipped; backend-changed and conflicts are reported as needing resolution.
